sections.h2: What are the options for selling a house fast in Sherman?
sections.html:
Sherman owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer, and the choice mostly comes down to the house's condition and the closing date you need. Sherman is the county seat of Grayson County, about 75 miles north of Dallas on U.S. Highway 75, so buyers here often include commuters, local workers and investors.

  • Agent listing: the widest buyer pool, with repairs, showings and a lender's timeline to manage.
  • Selling without an agent: you handle the contract, the buyer's questions and the paperwork with a title company.
  • Cash offer: a sale as-is, useful for a rental with tenants, an inherited house, or a property with deferred repairs.

Whichever route you pick, get a payoff figure from any lender and check the county tax account before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: Where can a Sherman seller check what nearby houses are worth?
sections.html:
Start with the Grayson County Appraisal District, which values every parcel in the county, and then ask a local title company for recent closed sales on streets near yours. An appraisal figure is a tax value, so it can differ from what a buyer will pay.

The appraisal district is at 205 N Travis Street in Sherman and can be reached at 903-893-9673, according to the city's property tax page. Its property database also shows the estimated amount of taxes on a given parcel, which is the quickest way to see what a buyer would inherit as a carrying cost.

sections.h2: How did Sherman grow, and why does it matter for a seller?
sections.html:
Sherman was laid out as the county seat in 1846 and spent its early decades as a merchandising and rail center. The Texas State Historical Association notes that a tornado on May 15, 1896 destroyed about fifty homes on the west side, and that large parts of the square were rebuilt after two fires in 1875.

The same entry credits Perrin Army Air Field, opened in 1941, with feeding postwar growth, and records oil discovered within the city limits in the 1950s. Austin College has been in Sherman since 1876. All of this left Sherman with housing stock from several eras, so a seller should expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at roofs, foundations and older wiring on anything built decades ago.

The city's own home page highlights semiconductor and optics manufacturing: a 300mm wafer fab opening, and a $650 million expansion by a local optics plant announced with its partner. These items reflect the city's recent push into chip making, and they bring jobs and housing demand for people who work at those plants.

For a seller the practical point is that employer announcements tend to bring buyers, including out-of-town buyers who want a quick, simple purchase. A clean listing price still matters, so compare any offer against what a neighbor's comparable sale actually closed for.

sections.h2: What property tax rates apply to a house in Sherman?
sections.html:
Four taxing units bill a typical Sherman home, and the city lists each rate per $100 of assessed value as of January 1, 2025. The city says its council adopted its own rate on September 2, 2025.

The city page listed a council vote on the 2026 rate for September 8, 2026, a date that has passed. For the rate on your latest bill, ask the Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector at 100 W Houston in Sherman, phone 903-892-8297. That office bills and collects the tax, while the appraisal district sets values.

sections.h2: When are Texas property taxes due, and who owes them after a sale?
sections.html:
Bills go out around October 1 and the usual deadline is January 31. The balance turns delinquent on February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest are added.

  • Taxes are measured as of January 1, and the lien attaches on that date.
  • The first-half installment option is due by November 30 and the second half by June 30 of the next year.
  • Owners 65 or older or disabled may pay in installments, and may qualify for a school tax ceiling.
  • The school homestead exemption is $140,000, with an extra $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled.

At closing the title company prorates the current year's tax between you and the buyer. Any prior-year balance is paid from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does Sherman handle neglected or blighted houses?
sections.html:
Sherman runs a Quality Neighborhoods Program aimed at blight and decay, and it removes substandard structures either with the owner's consent or by court order. A house that is vacant, damaged or otherwise condemned can fall within that program.

If your Sherman house is in poor condition, deal with any city notices before listing, since a buyer's lender may refuse a loan on a structure with open violations. A cash buyer will often take a house as-is, but the price will reflect the repair or demolition cost. The city's Neighborhood Services page is the place to ask about a specific property.

sections.h2: How is the deed recorded when a Sherman house sells?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the Grayson County Clerk, who keeps the real property records for every Sherman address. A deed can be recorded only if it is signed and acknowledged before a notary or another officer authorized to take acknowledgments.

The Texas Courts clerk manual prints a recording fee of $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each added page, along with separate records management and technology charges. Ask the clerk's office or your title company for the total on your document before closing day.

sections.h2: What if a tenant lives in the Sherman house?
sections.html:
A tenant can stay through a sale unless the lease or the law lets you end it, so a buyer may need to take the house with the lease in place. Texas requires at least three days' written notice to vacate unless the lease says otherwise, and the suit goes to justice court.

  • The tenant must be served at least four days before trial.
  • An appeal to county court is due within five days of the judgment.
  • A writ of possession becomes available six days after final judgment.

Investors who buy tenant-occupied houses can plan around these timelines, while an owner-occupant buyer usually wants the house empty at closing.

sections.h2: What if the Sherman house is inherited or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
A will can be probated within four years of death in Texas, and a muniment of title lets heirs show ownership without full administration when there are no debts other than liens. Texas's small estate affidavit covers estates of $75,000 or less excluding homestead and exempt property.

For foreclosure, a borrower can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of the default notice, and sales are held on the first Tuesday of the month after at least 21 days' notice. Selling before that date can protect your equity.

faqs.a: Sherman is in Grayson County, and it is the county seat. Property is valued by the Grayson County Appraisal District and taxes are collected by the county's tax assessor-collector.

faqs.q: What was Sherman's 2025 city tax rate?
faqs.a: The city lists $0.508000 per $100 of assessed value, adopted September 2, 2025. Ask the Grayson County tax office for the rate on your current bill.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sherman house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, but the lien stays with the house, so the balance, penalties and interest must be paid at or before closing. A title company will show the figure on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Does Sherman have a blight program that could affect my sale?
faqs.a: The city's Quality Neighborhoods Program removes substandard structures by consent or court order. If your house is in poor shape, contact Neighborhood Services before listing.

faqs.q: How quickly can I close on a Sherman house?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close faster than a financed sale because there is no loan underwriting. The actual timeline depends on title work, any probate needed, and whether liens must be cleared first.
